proposed_statement_changes.proposed: Establish or refute whether there is a universal constant \(c>0\) such that, for every \(0<\alpha\le 1/4\) and every unequal-clique experiment in the stated model, \[ \mathcal R_\alpha(w,q)\ge c\min\{1,\omega_\alpha(w,q)\}. \] The infimum defining \(\mathcal R_\alpha\) ranges over every measurable interval procedure, including procedures randomized by the independent external variable \(R\).
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The capped optimizer, the strengthened trimming dual, the unrestricted upper bound, the no-cap identity, and the exact consistency boundary are proved elsewhere in the frozen core.  The existing OEQ mixes those closed conclusions with the one unresolved assertion.  This correction narrows the question to the sole residual universal linear all-procedure lower bound.

proposed.statement: Establish or refute whether there is a universal constant \(c>0\) such that, for every \(0<\alpha\le 1/4\) and every unequal-clique experiment in the stated model, \[ \mathcal R_\alpha(w,q)\ge c\min\{1,\omega_\alpha(w,q)\}. \] The infimum defining \(\mathcal R_\alpha\) ranges over every measurable interval procedure, including procedures randomized by the independent external variable \(R\).
proposed.justification: The capped optimizer, the strengthened trimming dual, the unrestricted upper bound, the no-cap formula, and the exact consistency boundary are proved.  The remaining question is exactly whether the capped modulus supplies a universal linear lower bound for all measurable externally randomized intervals.
proposed.gap: The proved common-location no-reveal construction gives only a cubic lower bound.  A universal linear result still requires posterior or concentration-function control that is uniform over heterogeneous weighted erasure arrays, including moving-support boundaries and external interval randomization.
proposed.consumer: Closing this question would upgrade the proved dominance-aware upper modulus and cubic consistency converse to a sharp two-sided finite-confidence expected-length frontier.

obligation.what_is_open: Prove or refute a universal \(c>0\) for which \(\mathcal R_\alpha(w,q)\ge c\min\{1,\omega_\alpha(w,q)\}\) holds for every \(0<\alpha\le1/4\), every admissible unequal-clique array, and every measurable interval procedure, including procedures randomized by independent \(R\).
obligation.obstruction: The capped perturbation and its quadratic budget control divergence, but they do not by themselves lower-bound the posterior spread of the target under heterogeneous erasures.  The common-location no-reveal argument loses two powers of the modulus, while the product-Rademacher anti-concentration argument for the designated two-scale family uses its many identical size-two blocks and does not extend uniformly to arbitrary weights and reveal probabilities.
obligation.attempted: The KKT optimizer, the strengthened trimming comparison, the no-cap calculation, the minimax upper bound, and the cubic all-procedure lower bound have been completed.  Per the maximality directive, no unsupported posterior-spread assertion was retried; a general proof would still need a valid moving-support likelihood or Hellinger argument and a conversion to interval length that remains valid after conditioning on the data and the independent external randomizer.
obligation.partial_result: Let \(x=\log(1/\alpha)\).  The established results give \[ \omega_\alpha(w,q)\le\rho_\alpha(w,q)\le\frac52\omega_\alpha(w,q), \qquad \mathcal R_\alpha(w,q)\le5\min\{1,\omega_\alpha(w,q)\}, \] and, when no cap binds, \(\omega_\alpha(w,q)=\sqrt{Sx}\).  They also give the all-procedure converse \[ \mathcal R_\alpha(w,q)\ge \frac{\omega_\alpha(w,q)^3}{128x+8\omega_\alpha(w,q)^2}\ge\frac{\omega_\alpha(w,q)^3}{136x}. \] Consequently the fixed-confidence equivalence \(\mathcal R_\alpha\to0\Longleftrightarrow\omega_\alpha\to0\Longleftrightarrow\rho_0\to0\) is closed.  What remains open is only replacement of the cubic converse by a universal linear one at nonzero finite confidence.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The narrowed OEQ no longer uses the water-filling handle, the trimmed radius, the quadratic complexity, or the proved upper theorem in its own claim; its dependency and free-symbol metadata must match the residual lower-bound question.

prose_updates.tldr: Unequal clique sizes turn full-neighborhood All Treat and All Control exposures into independent nonidentical categorical reveals.  Exact enumeration sharpens each centered block Horvitz--Thompson increment to \(w_l/(2q_l)\), giving a clipped honest Bernstein interval with half-width \(\sqrt{S\log(2/\alpha)}+(M/6)\log(2/\alpha)\).  The capped water-filling optimizer is explicit, and the strengthened dual bounds are \(\omega_\alpha\le\rho_\alpha\le(5/2)\omega_\alpha\) and \(\omega_1\le\rho_0\le2\omega_1\), hence \(\mathcal R_\alpha\le5\min\{1,\omega_\alpha\}\).  A cubic lower bound valid for every measurable externally randomized interval proves the exact fixed-confidence consistency boundary \(\mathcal R_\alpha\to0\Longleftrightarrow\omega_\alpha\to0\Longleftrightarrow\rho_0\to0\).  A separate product-Rademacher anti-concentration argument gives the matching \(\Theta_\alpha(k^{-1/2})\) rate for the designated two-scale family only.  The sole unresolved sharp-frontier claim is a universal linear lower bound \(\mathcal R_\alpha\gtrsim\min\{1,\omega_\alpha\}\).  The pinned \(\texttt{szonszein/interference}\) version \(0.1.0\) diagnostic rejects nonclique neighborhoods and otherwise compares package labels with independently recomputed unanimous-block labels before returning any interval.

project_justification.gap: TchetgenTchetgenVanderWeele2012, Section 4.3, constructs Hoeffding intervals for binary allocation-strategy effects under two-stage Type-A partial interference, and RigdonHudgens2015 constructs exact confidence sets for those binary two-stage effects.  Neither treats the unequal-clique Bernoulli All Treat versus All Control minimax expected-length problem or proves its open universal linear water-filling lower frontier.  The exact consistency boundary is no longer a gap.
project_justification.niche: The design is the sole source of randomness, and the note separates two computable precision descriptions: the untrimmed Bernstein scales \(S\) and \(M\), and the dominance-aware capped or trimmed moduli \(\omega_\alpha\), \(\rho_\alpha\), and \(\rho_0\).  The capped modulus is necessary and sufficient for consistency even when \(S\not\to0\); its universal sharp linear finite-confidence lower interpretation remains open.
project_justification.fill: The proved contribution consists of the exact categorical block reduction with centered increment \(w_l/(2q_l)\), the observed-data clipped Horvitz--Thompson interval, bias-protected trimming, the KKT-certified water-filling optimizer, the bounds \(\omega_\alpha\le\rho_\alpha\le(5/2)\omega_\alpha\) and \(\omega_1\le\rho_0\le2\omega_1\), the unrestricted upper bound \(\mathcal R_\alpha\le5\min\{1,\omega_\alpha\}\), and a cubic lower bound covering all measurable externally randomized intervals.  These results prove the full consistency equivalence.  A product-Rademacher argument additionally closes the \(\Theta_\alpha(k^{-1/2})\) rate for the stated two-scale family, without being promoted to a universal converse.

sampling_model.design: Known independent unit-level \(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) assignment on a fixed partition into unequal disjoint cliques; the assignment distribution is the sole stochastic design object.
sampling_model.treatment: Within block \(l\), All Treat and All Control are mutually exclusive categorical events, each with probability \(q_l=2^{-r_l}\), and the block categories are independent across \(l\).
sampling_model.overlap: Every target exposure has known positive probability \(q_l\), which may vary across blocks and may vanish along triangular arrays; no uniform lower bound on \(q_l\) is imposed.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No superpopulation nuisance is estimated.  A unanimous block reveals exactly its corresponding fixed block mean; a trimmed-out block is covered by the deterministic bounded-outcome contrast allowance.

prose_updates.related_work: TchetgenTchetgenVanderWeele2012, Section 4.3, constructs Hoeffding intervals for binary allocation-strategy effects under two-stage Type-A partial interference, and RigdonHudgens2015 constructs exact confidence sets for those binary two-stage effects.  Neither treats this unequal-clique Bernoulli All Treat versus All Control minimax expected-length problem or proves the open water-filling lower frontier.  AronowSamii2017 provides the design--exposure--estimand framework and exposure-specific inverse weighting, while UganderKarrerBackstromKleinberg2013 documents exponentially small full-neighborhood exposure probabilities.  BasseAiroldi2018 gives a nonconcentration warning, UganderYin2023 changes the design to mitigate rare exposure, and KandirosHarshawSavje2026 studies design-based mean-squared-error criteria rather than all-interval expected length.  CaiLow2004 and ArmstrongKolesar2018 motivate modulus reasoning in Gaussian experiments but do not furnish the heterogeneous weighted-erasure interval-spread theorem needed here.  The present common-location argument proves the cubic converse needed for consistency, and the product-Rademacher calculation proves anti-concentration only for the designated two-scale family; neither is represented as the still-open universal linear converse.  The pinned \(\texttt{szonszein/interference}\) version \(0.1.0\) source labels its second output column by the complement of All Treat, so the diagnostic compares those labels with an independently recomputed unanimous All Control reference.
prose_updates.interpretation: The computable quantity \(\rho_0(w,q)\), equivalently \(\omega_1(w,q)\) up to the proved factor two, is the exact consistency diagnostic.  A rare block can keep \(S\) bounded away from zero while carrying so little causal weight that trimming it permits vanishing honest length.  At nonzero confidence the capped program supplies a certified upper modulus within factor five for expected length, and its uncapped regime reduces exactly to \(\sqrt{S\log(1/\alpha)}\).  The cubic converse rules out consistency whenever the capped modulus fails to vanish.  The matching linear lower rate is known here only for the designated two-scale family, not uniformly over heterogeneous arrays.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: For arbitrary heterogeneous arrays, the common-location no-reveal construction yields only \(\mathcal R_\alpha\ge\omega_\alpha^3/(128\log(1/\alpha)+8\omega_\alpha^2)\).  This is sufficient for the exact fixed-confidence consistency equivalence but may be much smaller than \(\omega_\alpha\).  The remaining sharp problem is therefore solely a universal linear weighted-erasure interval-spread converse, in both its capped global and no-dominance formulations.  A solution must control heterogeneous posterior or concentration-function spread, compact-support or moving-support boundaries, random revealed information, and independent external interval randomization.  The special product-Rademacher proof for the two-scale array does not supply this uniform step.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The proved results concern fixed potential outcomes in \([-1/2,1/2]\), known unequal disjoint clique blocks, and independent unit-level \(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) assignment.  The interval is a measurable function of \(D\) and known design quantities; its sharpened Bernstein term is \((M/6)\log(2/\alpha)\).  The KKT optimizer, trimming comparisons, cubic lower bound, and exact consistency boundary allow arbitrary independent external randomization of the reported interval.  The \(\Theta_\alpha(k^{-1/2})\) two-sided rate is asserted only for the specified two-scale family.  No universal sharp linear expected-length lower bound is claimed.  The software diagnostic rejects overlapping or nonclique neighborhoods, and on a clique input it withholds the interval unless package labels equal the independently recomputed target exposure labels.

statement_notes.justification: The optimizer, strengthened trimming dual, unrestricted upper bound, no-cap identity, and consistency theorem are closed; this question retains only the universal linear all-procedure lower bound.
statement_notes.gap: The cubic common-location converse and the special two-scale anti-concentration theorem do not yield posterior interval spread uniformly over arbitrary heterogeneous weighted erasure arrays.
statement_notes.consumer: A resolution would determine whether the computable capped modulus is the sharp nonzero finite-confidence expected-length scale for every admissible design.

proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(m\in\mathcal M_n(B)\) and a block \(B_l\).  By
\(\mathrm{ass{:}partition}\), the block is nonempty and the blocks are
pairwise disjoint.  By \(\mathrm{ass{:}balanced\text{-}bernoulli}\), every
one of the \(2^{r_l}\) assignments on \(B_l\) has probability
\(2^{-r_l}=q_l\).  Exactly one such assignment is all treated, exactly one
is all controlled, and all remaining assignments are mixed.  Therefore
\[
 \mathbb P_Z(A_l=1)=q_l,\qquad
 \mathbb P_Z(C_l=1)=q_l,\qquad
 \mathbb P_Z(H_l=1)=1-2q_l,
 \tag{1}
\]
and \(A_lC_l=0\) for every assignment.  Each triple
\((A_l,C_l,H_l)\) is a function only of \((Z_i:i\in B_l)\).  These
coordinate subvectors are independent for distinct blocks by
\(\mathrm{ass{:}partition}\) and
\(\mathrm{ass{:}balanced\text{-}bernoulli}\); hence the triples are
independent across \(l\).

Write \(u_l=\mu_l(a)\) and \(v_l=\mu_l(b)\).  The schedule is fixed by
\(\mathrm{ass{:}fixed\text{-}schedule}\), so \(u_l\) and \(v_l\) are
constants under \(P_Z\).  By
\(\mathrm{lem{:}observed\text{-}block\text{-}means}\), the observed block
mean equals \(u_l\) on \(\{A_l=1\}\) and equals \(v_l\) on
\(\{C_l=1\}\).  On a mixed assignment both multipliers in
\(\mathrm{def{:}block\text{-}ht}\) vanish.  Thus, pointwise on the whole
assignment space,
\[
 X_l=\frac{w_l}{q_l}\{A_lu_l-C_lv_l\}
 =
 \begin{cases}
   (w_l/q_l)u_l,&A_l=1,\\
   -(w_l/q_l)v_l,&C_l=1,\\
   0,&H_l=1.
 \end{cases}
 \tag{2}
\]
Using (1), mutual exclusion, and (2) gives
\[
 \mathbb E_ZX_l
 =q_l\frac{w_l}{q_l}u_l
  +q_l\left(-\frac{w_l}{q_l}v_l\right)
 =w_l\{\mu_l(a)-\mu_l(b)\}.
 \tag{3}
\]
Moreover,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \operatorname{Var}_Z(X_l)
 &\le \mathbb E_Z(X_l^2)\\
 &=q_l\frac{w_l^2}{q_l^2}u_l^2
   +q_l\frac{w_l^2}{q_l^2}v_l^2\\
 &=\frac{w_l^2}{q_l}(u_l^2+v_l^2)
 \le \frac{w_l^2}{2q_l}.
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{4}
\]
Here the first inequality is the identity
\(\operatorname{Var}(X)=\mathbb E(X^2)-(\mathbb EX)^2\le\mathbb E(X^2)\),
and the last inequality follows from
\(\mathrm{ass{:}bounded\text{-}outcomes}\) and
\(\mathrm{def{:}block\text{-}means}\), which imply
\(|u_l|,|v_l|\le 1/2\).  Summing (4) and using the definition of \(S\)
yields
\[
 \sum_{l=1}^L\operatorname{Var}_Z(X_l)
 \le \frac12\sum_{l=1}^L\frac{w_l^2}{q_l}
 =\frac S2.
 \tag{5}
\]

It remains to establish the sharper centered-increment bound required for
the downstream Bernstein radius.  Subtracting (3) from each of the three
values in (2) gives
\[
 X_l-\mathbb E_ZX_l=
 \begin{cases}
 w_l\{(q_l^{-1}-1)u_l+v_l\},&A_l=1,\\
 -w_l\{u_l+(q_l^{-1}-1)v_l\},&C_l=1,\\
 -w_l(u_l-v_l),&H_l=1.
 \end{cases}
 \tag{6}
\]
Because \(B_l\ne\varnothing\), one has \(r_l\ge1\), so
\(0<q_l=2^{-r_l}\le1/2\).  Consequently \(q_l^{-1}-1\ge0\), and the
outcome bounds applied to (6) show, on the all-treated and all-control
events respectively,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \left|w_l\{(q_l^{-1}-1)u_l+v_l\}\right|
 &\le \frac{w_l}{2}\{q_l^{-1}-1+1\}
 =\frac{w_l}{2q_l},\\
 \left|w_l\{u_l+(q_l^{-1}-1)v_l\}\right|
 &\le \frac{w_l}{2}\{1+q_l^{-1}-1\}
 =\frac{w_l}{2q_l}.
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{7}
\]
On the mixed event,
\[
 |w_l(u_l-v_l)|\le w_l\le\frac{w_l}{2q_l}.
 \tag{8}
\]
Equations (6)--(8) therefore prove the exact uniform envelope
\[
 |X_l-\mathbb E_ZX_l|\le\frac{w_l}{2q_l}\le\frac M2,
 \tag{9}
\]
which in particular implies the weaker displayed bound
\(|X_l-\mathbb E_ZX_l|\le w_l/q_l\le M\) in the frozen claim.  The
constant in (9) cannot be improved uniformly: the admissible schedule
\(u_l=v_l=1/2\) makes the centered value on \(\{A_l=1\}\) equal to
\(w_l/(2q_l)\).

For the required smallest unequal-block stress test, take
\(B_1=\{1\}\) and \(B_2=\{2,3\}\).  Among the two assignments on
\(B_1\), the category counts \((A_1,C_1,H_1)\) are \((1,1,0)\), while
among the four assignments on \(B_2\) the corresponding counts are
\((1,1,2)\).  Hence exhaustive enumeration of the \(2\cdot4=8\) joint
assignments gives probabilities \((1/2,1/2,0)\) for block one and
\((1/4,1/4,1/2)\) for block two, independently.  On every one of those
eight assignments, (2) and (6) give the realized and centered summands;
direct averaging reproduces (3)--(5), and (7)--(9) hold assignment by
assignment.  With \(u_l=v_l=1/2\), an all-treated assignment attains
equality in both (4) and (9), confirming the variance and increment
constants at this finite boundary instance.

Write \(y=\log(2/\alpha)=x+\log 2\).  Since \(0<\alpha\le1/4\),
\[
 x\ge 2\log 2,
 \qquad x\le y\le\frac32x.
\tag{1}
\]
By \(\mathrm{ass{:}partition}\), every block is nonempty.  Hence \(r_l\ge1\), so \(w_l=r_l/n>0\); also \(q_l>0\) by the declared range of \(q\).

For a budget \(z>0\), put
\[
 \mathcal D_z=\left\{\delta\in[0,1]^L:
       \sum_{l=1}^Lq_l\delta_l^2\le z\right\}.
\]
This is a nonempty compact subset of \(\mathbb R^L\), and the objective \(\delta\mapsto\sum_lw_l\delta_l\) is continuous, so a maximizer exists.  If \(z\ge\sum_lq_l\), the vector with every coordinate equal to one is feasible and is coordinatewise maximal; nonnegativity of the weights therefore makes it optimal.

Suppose now that \(0<z<\sum_lq_l\), and define
\[
 f(\lambda)=\sum_{l=1}^Lq_l
       \min\{1,\lambda w_l/q_l\}^2,
 \qquad \lambda\ge0.
\]
The function \(f\) is continuous, \(f(0)=0\), and \(f(\lambda)\to\sum_lq_l\) as \(\lambda\to\infty\).  Moreover, if \(0\le\lambda_1<\lambda_2\) and \(f(\lambda_2)<\sum_lq_l\), at least one coordinate is uncapped at \(\lambda_2\); positivity of \(w_l/q_l\) makes that coordinate strictly increase, while all other coordinates are nondecreasing.  Thus \(f(\lambda_1)<f(\lambda_2)\).  Continuity and this strict increase before the terminal plateau give a unique \(\lambda>0\) such that \(f(\lambda)=z\).  Set
\[
 delta_l^*=\min\{1,\lambda w_l/q_l\}.
\tag{2}
\]

We verify global optimality directly.  Let \(\delta\in\mathcal D_z\), let \(\mathcal C=\{l:\delta_l^*=1\}\), and let \(J=\mathcal C^c\).  For \(l\in J\), the identity \(w_l=q_l\delta_l^*/\lambda\) and the square inequality \((\delta_l-\delta_l^*)^2\ge0\) give
\[
 w_l(\delta_l-\delta_l^*)
 \le \frac{q_l}{2\lambda}
       \{\delta_l^2-(\delta_l^*)^2\}.
\tag{3}
\]
For \(l\in\mathcal C\), the cap condition gives \(w_l\ge q_l/\lambda\).  Since \(\delta_l-1\le0\) and \((\delta_l-1)^2\ge0\),
\[
 w_l(\delta_l-1)
 \le \frac{q_l}{\lambda}(\delta_l-1)
 \le \frac{q_l}{2\lambda}(\delta_l^2-1).
\tag{4}
\]
Summing (3)--(4), using \(\sum_lq_l(\delta_l^*)^2=z\), and using feasibility of \(\delta\), yields
\[
 \sum_lw_l(\delta_l-\delta_l^*)
 \le\frac1{2\lambda}
       \sum_lq_l\{\delta_l^2-(\delta_l^*)^2\}
 \le0.
\tag{5}
\]
Thus (2) is the global optimizer.  Equations (3)--(5), together with feasibility and complementary capping, are an explicit Karush--Kuhn--Tucker certificate.  Applying this argument with \(z=x\) proves the optimizer assertion in \(\mathrm{def{:}capped\text{-}modulus}\).

We next compare the capped and trimmed programs.  For every \(\delta\in\mathcal D_x\) and every \(J_0\subseteq\{1,\ldots,L\}\), the coordinate cap, Cauchy--Schwarz, and the quadratic constraint give
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \sum_lw_l\delta_l
 &\le \sum_{l\notin J_0}w_l+
       \sum_{l\in J_0}w_l\delta_l\\
 &\le \sum_{l\notin J_0}w_l+
 \left(\sum_{l\in J_0}\frac{w_l^2}{q_l}\right)^{1/2}
 \left(\sum_{l\in J_0}q_l\delta_l^2\right)^{1/2}\\
 &\le \sum_{l\notin J_0}w_l+
       \sqrt{x\sum_{l\in J_0}w_l^2/q_l}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{6}
\]
The right side of (6) is no larger than the corresponding candidate in \(\rho_\alpha\), because \(y\ge x\) and the linear maximum term is nonnegative.  Maximizing over \(\delta\) and then minimizing over \(J_0\) proves
\[
 \omega_\alpha(w,q)\le\rho_\alpha(w,q).
\tag{7}
\]

If \(x\ge\sum_lq_l\), the all-one vector is optimal, so \(\omega_\alpha=\sum_lw_l\).  Choosing \(J_0=\varnothing\) gives \(\rho_\alpha\le\sum_lw_l\), and (7) gives equality.  It remains to treat \(x<\sum_lq_l\).  Use (2) at budget \(x\), retain the sets \(\mathcal C,J\), and define
\[
 A=\sum_{l\in J}\frac{w_l^2}{q_l},
 \qquad Q=\sum_{l\in\mathcal C}q_l,
 \qquad B=\sum_{l\in\mathcal C}w_l,
 \qquad t=\lambda^{-1},
 \qquad p=x-Q.
\]
The active constraint, the objective value, and the cap inequalities imply
\[
 A=t^2p,
 \qquad \omega_\alpha=B+tp,
 \qquad B\ge tQ=t(x-p),
 \qquad \max_{l\in J}\frac{w_l}{q_l}<t.
\tag{8}
\]
Choosing \(J_0=J\) in \(\rho_\alpha\) and using its frozen coefficient \(y/3\) gives the bound
\[
 \rho_\alpha
 \le B+t\sqrt{yp}+\frac y3t.
\tag{9}
\]
This bound remains valid, and only becomes looser, after replacing that coefficient by the directed sharper coefficient \(y/6\).  From \((\sqrt p-\sqrt y/2)^2\ge0\),
\[
 \sqrt{yp}\le p+\frac y4,
 \qquad
 \sqrt{yp}+\frac y3\le p+\frac{7y}{12}
 \le p+\frac{7x}{8},
\tag{10}
\]
where the last inequality uses (1).  On the other hand, (8) gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \frac52(B+tp)-\left(B+t\sqrt{yp}+\frac y3t\right)
 &=\frac32B+t\left(\frac52p-\sqrt{yp}-\frac y3\right)\\
 &\ge t\left(\frac32x+p-\sqrt{yp}-\frac y3\right)\\
 &\ge \frac{5}{8}tx>0.
\end{aligned}
\tag{11}
\]
Combining (9)--(11) proves the sharpened finite-confidence comparison
\[
 \rho_\alpha(w,q)\le\frac52\omega_\alpha(w,q).
\tag{12}
\]
In particular, it proves the stated weaker constant four.

Finally, repeat (6) with quadratic budget one to obtain \(\omega_1\le\rho_0\).  If \(1\ge\sum_lq_l\), the all-one argument gives equality.  Otherwise repeat (8) with \(x=1\).  Then \(0\le p\le1\), \(B\ge t(1-p)\), and
\[
 \omega_1=B+tp\ge t,
 \qquad
 \rho_0\le B+\sqrt A=B+t\sqrt p\le B+t\le2\omega_1.
\tag{13}
\]
Thus
\[
 \omega_1(w,q)\le\rho_0(w,q)\le2\omega_1(w,q),
\tag{14}
\]
which in particular proves the stated weaker constant three.  Equations (2), (5), (7), (12), and (14) prove all assertions, including the two strengthened constants required for downstream use.

Fix \(0<\alpha\le1/4\), and put \(x=\log(1/\alpha)\), which is a positive constant along the triangular array.  For this proof, write
\[
 \omega_z(w,q)=\max\left\{\sum_lw_l\delta_l:
 0\le\delta_l\le1,\ \sum_lq_l\delta_l^2\le z\right\}.
\tag{15}
\]
Thus \(\omega_\alpha=\omega_x\), while \(\omega_1\) is the budget-one program in \(\mathrm{lem{:}capped\text{-}trimming\text{-}duality}\).  Since \(x\ge\log4>1\), inclusion of feasible sets gives \(\omega_1\le\omega_x\).  Conversely, if \(\delta\) is feasible for \(\omega_x\), then \(\delta/\sqrt x\in[0,1]^L\) and
\[
 \sum_lq_l(\delta_l/\sqrt x)^2\le1.
\]
The definition of \(\omega_1\), followed by multiplication by \(\sqrt x\), therefore gives
\[
 \omega_1(w,q)\le\omega_\alpha(w,q)
 \le\sqrt x\,\omega_1(w,q).
\tag{16}
\]
The sharpened budget-one comparison proved in \(\mathrm{lem{:}capped\text{-}trimming\text{-}duality}\) is
\[
 \omega_1(w,q)\le\rho_0(w,q)\le2\omega_1(w,q).
\tag{17}
\]
Because \(x\) is fixed, (16)--(17) imply, row by row along every triangular array,
\[
 \omega_\alpha(w^{(n)},q^{(n)})\longrightarrow0
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \rho_0(w^{(n)},q^{(n)})\longrightarrow0.
\tag{18}
\]

By \(\mathrm{thm{:}trimmed\text{-}upper}\), there is an interval in \(\mathfrak C_\alpha\) whose length is at most \(2\min\{1,\rho_\alpha\}\) for every fixed schedule.  Taking its worst-case expected length and then the infimum over honest procedures, and using the sharpened finite-confidence comparison (12), gives
\[
 \mathcal R_\alpha(w,q)
 \le2\min\{1,\rho_\alpha(w,q)\}
 \le2\rho_\alpha(w,q)
 \le5\omega_\alpha(w,q).
\tag{19}
\]
Consequently, \(\omega_\alpha\to0\) implies \(\mathcal R_\alpha\to0\).  For the converse, the already established \(\mathrm{lem{:}capped\text{-}erasure\text{-}consistency\text{-}lower}\) gives at every row
\[
 \mathcal R_\alpha(w,q)
 \ge \frac{\omega_\alpha(w,q)^3}{136x}.
\tag{20}
\]
If \(\mathcal R_\alpha\to0\), (20) implies
\[
 0\le\omega_\alpha(w,q)
 \le\{136x\,\mathcal R_\alpha(w,q)\}^{1/3}\longrightarrow0.
\tag{21}
\]
Combining (18), (19), and (21) proves
\[
 \mathcal R_\alpha(w^{(n)},q^{(n)})\to0
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \omega_\alpha(w^{(n)},q^{(n)})\to0
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \rho_0(w^{(n)},q^{(n)})\to0.
\tag{22}
\]

It remains to compare this exact boundary with \(S\).  For every vector feasible for \(\omega_\alpha\), positivity of \(q_l\), Cauchy--Schwarz, and the quadratic constraint yield
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \sum_lw_l\delta_l
 &=\sum_l\frac{w_l}{\sqrt{q_l}}\sqrt{q_l}\delta_l\\
 &\le\left(\sum_l\frac{w_l^2}{q_l}\right)^{1/2}
       \left(\sum_lq_l\delta_l^2\right)^{1/2}
 \le\sqrt{xS}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{23}
\]
Maximization gives \(\omega_\alpha\le\sqrt{xS}\), so (19) gives
\[
 \mathcal R_\alpha(w,q)\le5\sqrt{xS}.
\tag{24}
\]
Thus \(S^{(n)}\to0\) is sufficient.

To prove that it is not necessary, construct an explicit valid unequal-clique array.  For every integer \(k\ge1\), let
\[
 n_k=2k\,2^k
\]
and partition the population into one block of size \(2k\) and \(n_k-2k\) singleton blocks.  The partition condition holds exactly, and \(\mathrm{ass{:}balanced\text{-}bernoulli}\) gives for the large block
\[
 w_{\mathrm{big}}=\frac{2k}{n_k}=2^{-k},
 \qquad q_{\mathrm{big}}=2^{-2k},
 \qquad \frac{w_{\mathrm{big}}^2}{q_{\mathrm{big}}}=1.
\tag{25}
\]
Every singleton has \(w_l=1/n_k\) and \(q_l=1/2\).  Hence
\[
 S^{(n_k)}
 =1+\frac{2(n_k-2k)}{n_k^2}
 \longrightarrow1,
\tag{26}
\]
so this array does not satisfy \(S^{(n_k)}\to0\).

On the other hand, in \(\mathrm{def{:}trimmed\text{-}radius}\) choose \(J_k\) to contain all singleton blocks and omit only the large block.  With \(y=\log(2/\alpha)\), the frozen \(y/3\) linear coefficient gives
\[
 \rho_\alpha(w^{(n_k)},q^{(n_k)})
 \le 2^{-k}
 +\sqrt{\frac{2y(n_k-2k)}{n_k^2}}
 +\frac{2y}{3n_k}
 \longrightarrow0.
\tag{27}
\]
The directed replacement of that coefficient by \(y/6\) only decreases the left-side candidate, so (27) remains valid after that repair.  Applying \(\mathrm{thm{:}trimmed\text{-}upper}\) gives
\[
 \mathcal R_\alpha(w^{(n_k)},q^{(n_k)})
 \le2\rho_\alpha(w^{(n_k)},q^{(n_k)})\longrightarrow0.
\tag{28}
\]
Equations (26)--(28) are a concrete triangular-array witness that \(S\to0\) is not necessary.  This completes every assertion.

proposed.statement:
Let \(0<\alpha\le1/4\), \(x=\log(1/\alpha)\), and \(y=\log(2/\alpha)\).  The optimizer in \(\mathrm{def{:}capped\text{-}modulus}\) is the stated water-filling vector.  Moreover,
\[
 \omega_\alpha(w,q)\le\rho_\alpha(w,q)\le4\omega_\alpha(w,q),
 \qquad
 \omega_1(w,q)\le\rho_0(w,q)\le3\omega_1(w,q),
\]
where \(\omega_1\) denotes the same capped program with quadratic budget one.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The water-filling uniqueness proof uses the strict positivity of every block weight, which follows from the nonempty-block partition assumption; this dependency must be explicit.

proofs.proof_tex:
The total population size is \(2k+4k=6k\).  Therefore a size-two
block has
\[
 w_l=\frac2{6k}=\frac1{3k},\qquad q_l=2^{-2}=\frac14,
\]
and a size-four block has
\[
 w_l=\frac4{6k}=\frac2{3k},\qquad q_l=2^{-4}=\frac1{16},
\]
where the reveal probabilities follow from balanced independent
assignment.  Direct substitution in the definitions of \(S\) and
\(M\) gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 S
 &=k\frac{(1/(3k))^2}{1/4}
   +k\frac{(2/(3k))^2}{1/16}
   =\frac4{9k}+\frac{64}{9k}
   =\frac{68}{9k},\\
 M
 &=\max\left\{\frac{1/(3k)}{1/4},
                \frac{2/(3k)}{1/16}\right\}
   =\frac{32}{3k}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{15}
\]
Consequently
\[
 \frac{M\sqrt{\log(1/\alpha)}}{\sqrt S}
 =\frac{32\sqrt{\log(1/\alpha)}}{\sqrt{68k}}
 \longrightarrow0
\tag{16}
\]
for fixed \(\alpha\).  The hypothesis of
\(\mathrm{thm{:}no\text{-}dominance\text{-}upper}\) therefore holds
eventually, and substitution of (15) in that theorem gives the stated
upper bound.  Together with
\(\mathrm{lem{:}two\text{-}scale\text{-}rademacher\text{-}lower}\),
the same calculation also yields the directive's specialized sharp
conclusion
\[
 \mathcal R_\alpha(w,q)=\Theta_\alpha(k^{-1/2})
\]
for every fixed \(0<\alpha\le1/4\).  This invocation is confined to
the present two-scale family and makes no assertion about either
universal linear lower-bound open question.

Finally, the cap breakpoints in
\(\mathrm{def{:}capped\text{-}modulus}\) are \(q_l/w_l\).  They equal
\[
 \frac{1/4}{1/(3k)}=\frac{3k}{4},
 \qquad
 \frac{1/16}{2/(3k)}=\frac{3k}{32}.
\tag{17}
\]
Because \(r\mapsto2^{-r}\) is injective on positive integers, a
single common block size cannot yield both \(1/4\) and \(1/16\); (17)
also shows directly that it cannot yield both breakpoint values.

added_lemmas.statement:
For the family \(B^{(k)}\) containing \(k\) blocks of size two and \(k\) blocks of size four, every \(0<\alpha\le 1/4\) and every integer \(k\ge64\) satisfy
\[
 \mathcal R_\alpha(w,q)\ge \frac{1}{192\sqrt{k}}.
\]
This lower bound applies to the full class of measurable honest interval procedures, including procedures externally randomized by \(R\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix \(0<\alpha\le1/4\), an integer \(k\ge64\), and an arbitrary
\(\Gamma\in\mathfrak C_\alpha\).  Index the \(k\) size-two blocks by
\(j=1,\ldots,k\).  In the hard schedules from
\(\mathrm{def{:}hard\text{-}subexperiment\text{-}embedding}\), put
\[
 V_j=\frac{\varepsilon_j}{2},\qquad
 P(\varepsilon_j=1)=P(\varepsilon_j=-1)=\frac12
 \quad(j=1,\ldots,k),
\tag{1}
\]
independently, and set \(V_l=1/2\) deterministically on every size-four
block.  This product law is used only to average the pointwise coverage
and risk inequalities furnished by
\(\mathrm{lem{:}hard\text{-}subexperiment\text{-}embedding}\); every
schedule in its support is a fixed member of \(\mathcal M_n(B^{(k)})\).
For a size-two block, balanced independent Bernoulli assignment gives
\[
 q_j=\frac14,\qquad w_j=\frac1{3k}.
\tag{2}
\]
Let \(K_j\) be its all-treated reveal indicator and let
\[
 N=\sum_{j=1}^k(1-K_j).
\tag{3}
\]
By the independent erasure reduction in
\(\mathrm{lem{:}hard\text{-}subexperiment\text{-}embedding}\), the
variables \(K_j\) are independent \(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/4)\)
variables, independent of the signs in (1).  Consequently
\[
 N\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(k,3/4),\qquad
 \mathbb EN=\frac{3k}{4},\qquad
 \operatorname{Var}(N)=\frac{3k}{16}.
\tag{4}
\]

Write \(\Lambda=\Lambda_\Gamma(O,R)\) for the randomized interval in
the erasure experiment constructed in
\(\mathrm{def{:}hard\text{-}subexperiment\text{-}embedding}\), and put
\(L_\Lambda=\operatorname{len}(\Lambda)\).  Conditional on \((O,R)\),
the revealed size-two signs are fixed, the size-four contribution is
fixed, and the \(N\) unrevealed size-two signs remain independent fair
Rademacher variables: the observation contains only
\((K_j,K_jV_j)\), while the declared external randomizer \(R\) is
independent of the assignment and of the prior signs.  Since
\(\theta=\sum_lw_lV_l\) on these schedules, its conditional law thus
has the form
\[
 c(O)+\frac1{6k}\sum_{s=1}^{N}\xi_s,
\tag{5}
\]
where, conditionally on \((O,R)\), the \(\xi_s\) are independent fair
Rademacher variables and \(c(O)\) is fixed.  Adjacent support points in
(5) are separated by \(1/(3k)\).

We next prove the elementary atom bound needed below.  If
\(S_N=\sum_{s=1}^N\xi_s\), then its largest atom is
\[
 p_N=2^{-N}\binom{N}{\lfloor N/2\rfloor}.
\]
For \(N=2m\), factorial cancellation gives
\[
 p_{2m}=4^{-m}\binom{2m}{m}
       =\prod_{s=1}^m\left(1-\frac1{2s}\right).
\]
The inequalities \(\log(1-u)\le-u\) for \(0<u<1\) and
\(\sum_{s=1}^m s^{-1}\ge\int_1^{m+1}t^{-1}\,dt=\log(m+1)\) imply
\[
 p_{2m}\le(m+1)^{-1/2}\le\sqrt{\frac2{2m}}.
\tag{6}
\]
For \(N=2m+1\),
\[
 p_{2m+1}=\frac{2m+1}{2m+2}p_{2m}
 \le(m+1)^{-1/2}
 \le\sqrt{\frac2{2m+1}}.
\tag{7}
\]
The case \(N=1\) also satisfies (7).  Hence, for every \(N\ge1\),
\[
 p_N\le\sqrt{\frac2N}.
\tag{8}
\]

An interval of length \(u\) contains at most \(3ku+1\) points of a
lattice with spacing \(1/(3k)\).  It follows from (5) and (8) that on
\(N\ge k/2\), conditionally on \((O,R)\),
\[
 P\{\theta\in\Lambda\mid O,R\}
 \le (3kL_\Lambda+1)\sqrt{\frac2N}.
\tag{9}
\]
In particular, on
\[
 \mathcal A=\left\{N\ge\frac k2,\quad
 L_\Lambda<\frac1{48\sqrt{k}}\right\},
\]
equation (9) and \(k\ge64\) give
\[
 P\{\theta\in\Lambda\mid O,R\}
 \le\left(\frac{\sqrt{k}}{16}+1\right)\frac2{\sqrt{k}}
 =\frac18+\frac2{\sqrt{k}}
 \le\frac38.
\tag{10}
\]
On the event \(N<k/2\), equation (4) gives
\(|N-\mathbb EN|>k/4\), and hence
\(\mathbf 1\{N<k/2\}\le16(N-\mathbb EN)^2/k^2\).  Taking
expectations and using the variance in (4) yields
\[
 P\left(N<\frac k2\right)
 \le \frac{3k/16}{(k/4)^2}
 =\frac3k\le\frac3{64}.
\tag{11}
\]

The pointwise honesty of \(\Gamma\), averaged over the product law
(1), and the coverage identity in
\(\mathrm{lem{:}hard\text{-}subexperiment\text{-}embedding}\) imply
\[
 P\{\theta\in\Lambda\}\ge1-\alpha\ge\frac34.
\tag{12}
\]
On \(\mathcal A\) the conditional coverage is at most \(3/8\) by
(10), and outside \(\mathcal A\) it is at most one.  Therefore
\[
 \frac34
 \le P\{\theta\in\Lambda\}
 \le\frac38+P\left(N<\frac k2\right)
      +P\left(L_\Lambda\ge\frac1{48\sqrt{k}}\right).
\]
Using (11),
\[
 P\left(L_\Lambda\ge\frac1{48\sqrt{k}}\right)
 \ge\frac38-\frac3{64}=\frac{21}{64}\ge\frac14.
\tag{13}
\]
Consequently
\[
 \mathbb E L_\Lambda
 \ge\frac1{48\sqrt{k}}\,
     P\left(L_\Lambda\ge\frac1{48\sqrt{k}}\right)
 \ge\frac1{192\sqrt{k}}.
\tag{14}
\]
The expected-length identity and supremum inequality in
\(\mathrm{lem{:}hard\text{-}subexperiment\text{-}embedding}\) show
that the worst fixed-schedule risk of the original \(\Gamma\) is at
least the product-prior average in (14).  Since \(\Gamma\) was an
arbitrary member of \(\mathfrak C_\alpha\), taking the infimum in
\(\mathrm{def{:}length\text{-}risk}\) proves
\[
 \mathcal R_\alpha(w,q)\ge\frac1{192\sqrt{k}}.
\]
The construction and conditioning retained the independent coordinate
\(R\) throughout, so the argument covers every externally randomized
measurable interval in the decision class.
added_lemmas.justification: A product-Rademacher prior on the size-two stratum supplies a fully finite-sample lower bound for the concrete heterogeneous triangular array.
added_lemmas.gap: The argument is deliberately specialized to this two-scale family and does not settle either universal linear lower-bound open question.
added_lemmas.consumer: Together with the no-dominance upper bound, this lemma certifies the fixed-confidence order of the minimax expected length in the two-scale example.

proposed.statement:
Let \(B^{(k)}\) contain \(k\) blocks of size two and \(k\) blocks of
size four, so \(n=6k\).  The two strata have
\((w_l,q_l)=(1/(3k),1/4)\) and
\((w_l,q_l)=(2/(3k),1/16)\), respectively, and
\[
 S=\frac{68}{9k},\qquad M=\frac{32}{3k},\qquad
 \frac{M\sqrt{\log(1/\alpha)}}{\sqrt S}
 =\frac{32\sqrt{\log(1/\alpha)}}{\sqrt{68k}}.
\]
Thus, for every fixed \(0<\alpha\le1/4\), the no-dominance condition
holds for all sufficiently large \(k\).  With \(C_1\) denoting the
universal constant in
\(\mathrm{thm{:}no\text{-}dominance\text{-}upper}\),
\[
 \mathcal R_\alpha(w,q)
 \le C_1\min\left\{1,
       \sqrt{\frac{68\log(1/\alpha)}{9k}}\right\}
 =O_\alpha(k^{-1/2}).
\]
The two water-filling breakpoints \(q_l/w_l\) are \(3k/4\) and
\(3k/32\).  No common block size can reproduce both reveal
probabilities, or both breakpoints.
proposed.justification: This concrete triangular array makes the heterogeneous theorem refutable through exact constants and a nondegenerate two-scale exposure structure.
proposed.gap: The inherited equal-block formula collapses all blocks to one reveal probability and one cap threshold, so it cannot deliver this two-stratum prediction.
proposed.consumer: A simulation study and the package diagnostic can check the predicted \(k^{-1/2}\) confidence-length curve separately within the two exposure strata.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Wire the directive-mandated specialized product-Rademacher lower bound into the concrete two-scale proposition's proof spine without changing the frozen claim.
